title: Completed stalk transport is compatible with its finite reductions
statement: Fix $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$ and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$, as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $X_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\Phi,g_\gamma$ be the scheme and geometric Frobenii of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Let $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ be derived-complete integral constructible [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] with $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$. Fix $m\ge1$, $y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})$ and a geometric point $\bar y:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ with $\Phi^m\bar y=\bar y$. The integral stalk is $S(K)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar y^*K)$, using completed pullback and [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]; write $L\bar y_n^*$ for finite-coefficient pullback along the same scheme map $\bar y$, and put $S_n(K_n)=\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar y_n^*K_n)$. The canonical reduction identifications of [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible] and [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction] identify $S(K)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_n$ with $S_n(K_n)$, naturally in $K$. Use the fixed-point normalization of [def-trf-frobenius-operators]: at level $n$, $\tau_{y,m,n}=(\kappa^{(m)}_{K_n})_{\bar y}\circ\iota_{K_n}$, where $\iota_{K_n}$ is the pullback-composition identification induced by $\Phi^m\bar y=\bar y$, and the integral $\tau_{y,m}$ is their specified derived-limit realization. Then these reduction identifications carry the reduction of $\tau_{y,m}:S(K)\to S(L(g_\gamma^m)^*K)$ to $\tau_{y,m,n}$. They commute with every transition $A_b\to A_a$ and with morphisms of integral objects.

proof.text:
Put $R=\mathcal O_E$, $h=\Phi^m$, $g=g_\gamma^m$, and $Y=\bar y:s\to X$. For an integral object $M$ write $M_n=M\otimes_R^LA_n$ and $S(M)=\Gamma(s,LY^*M)$, using [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. By [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible], $LY^*M$ is integral constructible and its canonical reduction is $LY_n^*M_n$. Compose this reduction map with the natural isomorphism of [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction] at $N=LY^*M$ to obtain
$$\alpha_{M,n}:S(M)\otimes_R^LA_n\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,LY_n^*M_n).$$
These are precisely the two canonical comparisons specified in the item. They are natural in integral morphisms $M\to M'$. The same construction applies to $Lh^*K$ and $Lg^*K$, which are integral constructible by the pullback-preservation assertion. All schemes in these applications have $\ell$ invertible, since they have characteristic $p\ne\ell$.

proof.text:
Put $P_n=S_n(K_n)$ and $Q_n=S_n(Lg_n^*K_n)$. Their quotient comparisons $\sigma_P:r_{b,a}P_b\simeq P_a$ and $\sigma_Q:r_{b,a}Q_b\simeq Q_a$, where $r_{b,a}=-\otimes_{A_b}^LA_a$, come from the quotient tower [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], monoidality [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and finite point sections [lem-trf-point-sections-finite-reduction]. The point complexes are bounded: finite pullback is exact by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Thus the last theorem applies, including its three-index cocycle, without assuming $A_a$ flat over $A_b$. Write $I_n=\iota_{K_n}$ and $B_n=S_n(\kappa^{(m)}_{K_n})$, so $\tau_n=B_nI_n$ by [def-trf-frobenius-operators]. Apply [lem-trf-fixed-stalk-identification-reduction] with $N=b,j=a,h=\Phi^m,K=K_b,t=s$. Its hypotheses hold: $h$ is a $k$-endomorphism, $hY=Y$ is assumed, and $K_b$ is finite-Tor constructible. It gives $\sigma_Hr_{b,a}(I_b)=I_a\sigma_P$, where $H_n=S_n(Lh_n^*K_n)$. The square of [lem-trf-frobenius-coefficient-reduction-coherence], after point pullback and natural finite point sections, gives $\sigma_Qr_{b,a}(B_b)=B_a\sigma_H$. Therefore
$$\sigma_Qr_{b,a}(\tau_b)=\tau_a\sigma_P.$$
This proves compatibility of the specified finite transports, not merely existence of unrelated maps with the same source and target.

source.place: clause *(4)*: reduction of the completed stalk and of its normalized transport, before composing with a coefficient morphism

proof.text:
The completed pullback formula of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] gives $LY^*K$ as the specified functorial derived limit of $(LY_n^*K_n)_n$. For the target, apply [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] to $Y:s\to X$ followed by $g:X\to X$. It identifies $LY^*Lg^*K$ with the completed pullback along $gY$, with reductions exactly $LY_n^*Lg_n^*K_n$. Thus its defining limit has these finite terms and the same quotient transitions. Point sections carry both sheaf limits to module limits. To check this on the actual model, [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] supplies the functorial shifted cone of $1-t$ on products, and [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] says termwise sections preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Products of module sheaves are evaluated componentwise; finite direct sums and differentials are likewise evaluated componentwise. Consequently sections carry $(x_n)\mapsto(x_n-t_nx_{n+1})$ and its shifted cone to precisely the same formula on section complexes, including the projections. Hence
$$S(K)\simeq R\!\varprojlim P_n,\qquad S(Lg^*K)\simeq R\!\varprojlim Q_n.$$
Write their actual projections as $p_n,q_n$. Under these identifications the integral transport in the item is its stipulated derived-limit realization of $(\tau_n)$, so $q_n\tau_{y,m}=\tau_np_n$. No construction of a lift from an arbitrary family of maps in a triangulated category is required.

source.place: clause *(4)*: reduction of the completed stalk and of its normalized transport, before composing with a coefficient morphism

proof.text:
We identify the adjoints of these projections with the canonical comparisons of step 1. On $s$, the pulled-back quotient towers are normalized: apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the quotient normalizations of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Their coherent counits are isomorphisms by [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]. The adjunction and projection normalization of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] say that the counit at level $n$ is the scalar-extension adjoint of the actual limit projection. Thus these are the canonical pullback-reduction maps of [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible], rather than arbitrary isomorphisms between the same objects. Use the normalized comparison $\chi_N$ of [lem-trf-point-reduction-unit-normalization]. It satisfies $\operatorname{Res}(\chi_N)\eta_{\Gamma N}=\Gamma(\eta_N)$. If $e:N\otimes_B^L B_n\to N_n$ is adjoint to $c$, then $\operatorname{Res}(e)\eta_N=c$. Applying sections and substituting gives $\operatorname{Res}(\Gamma(e)\chi_N)\eta_{\Gamma N}=\Gamma(c)$. The adjunction of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] therefore identifies $\Gamma(e)\chi_N$ with the adjunct of $\Gamma(c)$, for every derived morphism $c$. Therefore $\alpha_{K,n}$ is adjoint to $p_n$, and
$$\beta_n:=S_n(\rho_{g,K,n})\circ\alpha_{Lg^*K,n}$$
is adjoint to $q_n$. The comparison for the target is the one of step 3 because the integral composition theorem there identifies its reductions with finite pullback composition.

source.place: clause *(4)*: reduction of the completed stalk and of its normalized transport, before composing with a coefficient morphism

proof.text:
Apply the natural adjunction bijection of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] on the one-object site, for $R\to A_n$, to the equality $q_n\tau_{y,m}=\tau_np_n$ of step 3. The adjoint of its left side is $\beta_n\circ(\tau_{y,m}\otimes_R^LA_n)$, by naturality in the source. The adjoint of its right side is $\tau_n\circ\alpha_{K,n}$, by naturality in the target. Equality of the adjoints is exactly
$$\beta_n\circ(\tau_{y,m}\otimes_R^LA_n)=\tau_{y,m,n}\circ\alpha_{K,n}.$$
Step 4 identified both comparisons with those in the statement, including reduction of $Lg^*K$ on the target. This proves the asserted reduction square for every $n\ge1$.

source.place: clause *(4)*: reduction of the completed stalk and of its normalized transport, before composing with a coefficient morphism

proof.text: For successive quotients $R\to A_b\to A_a$, use [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization]. Its associativity identifies two successive scalar extensions with the direct one and identifies their composite unit with the direct unit. The adjunction in [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] then identifies both $\sigma_P(\alpha_{K,b}\otimes_{A_b}^LA_a)$ and $\alpha_{K,a}$ with the same projection $p_a$: the composite of $p_b$ and the transition to level $a$ is $p_a$. Here the finite sections comparison is the one of [lem-trf-point-sections-finite-reduction], natural and compatible with successive reductions; its unit normalization is supplied by [lem-trf-point-reduction-unit-normalization], so the adjunction calculation of step 4 applies also to the finite comparison. The identical argument gives $\sigma_Q(\beta_b\otimes_{A_b}^LA_a)=\beta_a$. Together with step 2 these identities prove compatibility with all transitions, including equal indices. For an integral morphism $f:K\to K'$, the quotient tower is functorial by [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]; the natural $\kappa^{(m)}$ of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison] and natural pullback composition of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] give the natural finite transport squares. The specified functorial limit realizes these squares, and the canonical counits and point-sections comparisons are natural. Thus $S(Lg^*f)\tau_{y,m,K}=\tau_{y,m,K'}S(f)$, and every reduction square above commutes with $f$.

Reused existing finite Frobenius/fixed-stalk coherence, integral composition, canonical normalized-system counits and point-sections reduction. No statement change and no new nodes. lean.note: Uses the published LocalFrobeniusTransport finiteNormalized and integralNormalized, not a new choice of transport. The target uses canonical composite-pullback coordinates. Identity-induced localization-size comparisons reconcile the small point-fibre and standard coefficient-adjunction derived categories, preserving the site and coefficient universes. ReductionStatement unfolds the reduction square, all quotient transitions (in normalized adjoint form), and naturality in every integral morphism; all positive exponents are successors. Good representatives are universally quantified, not extra restrictions on K.
